turns: Turn 01: Initial FNOL report received: pipe burst in master bathroom.
Turn 02: Field adjuster assigned: T. Jenkins.
Turn 03: Contacted insured Arthur Pendelton to schedule site visit.
Turn 04: Arrived on site; water standing on hardwood floor.
Turn 05: Moisture readings in master bath floor register 99%.
Turn 06: Water mitigation crew from ServPro on site with dehumidifiers.
Turn 07: Plumber invoice reviewed: emergency pipe clamp installed.
Turn 08: Plumber report states copper pipe failed due to sudden freeze.
Turn 09: Thermostat history checked: heat was maintained at 68F.
Turn 10: Drywall inspection shows moisture wicking up 24 inches.
Turn 11: Baseboards removed in master bedroom for drying.
Turn 12: Subfloor moisture meter readings down to 45%.
Turn 13: Subfloor inspection shows no prior rot or decay.
Turn 14: Contractor estimate received for drywall replacement: $3,200.
Turn 15: Contractor estimate for hardwood floor refinishing: $7,000.
Turn 16: Plumbing repair bill verified: $1,200.
Turn 17: Water mitigation bill audited: $3,600.
Turn 18: Total verified damages across trades equal $15,000.
Turn 19: Cross-referenced policy declarations page for HO-0304.
Turn 20: Verified endorsement HO-0304 is in effect with 03-24 edition.
Turn 21: Confirmed sudden plumbing rupture is covered under Section I.
Turn 22: Verified exclusions E-15 through E-18 do not apply.
Turn 23: Confirmed no flood, no continuous seepage, no sewer backup.
Turn 24: Insured provided receipts for emergency lodging.
Turn 25: Adjuster reviewed photos of ruptured copper pipe elbow.
Turn 26: Confirmed rupture is classic freeze-burst mechanical failure.
Turn 27: Mitigation certificate of completion signed by homeowner.
Turn 28: Contractor confirmed scope of work aligns with estimate.
Turn 29: Final inspection confirmed dwelling is dry and ready for repair.
Turn 30: Adjuster recommends full approval for sudden freeze pipe burst.

destroyed_fact: Turn 07 statement: Subcontractor noted homeowner admitted discovering hairline foundation cracks and slow subfloor seepage 18 months prior to policy inception.
turns: Turn 01: Initial FNOL report: severe basement water accumulation.
Turn 02: Field adjuster assigned: M. Vance.
Turn 03: Insured states water entered basement after weekend rain.
Turn 04: Arrived on site; pump operating in basement sump pit.
Turn 05: Moisture readings on south basement wall exceed 95%.
Turn 06: Water mitigation company installing drying fans.
Turn 07: CRITICAL ADMISSION: Subcontractor noted homeowner admitted discovering hairline foundation cracks and slow subfloor seepage 18 months prior to policy inception.
Turn 08: Sump pump tested; pump operates but check valve stuck.
Turn 09: Basement carpet removed due to mold growth.
Turn 10: Drywall cut away 2 feet above floor line.
Turn 11: Concrete foundation wall inspected behind drywall.
Turn 12: Multiple step fractures visible in masonry blocks.
Turn 13: Moisture continuing to weep through exterior masonry.
Turn 14: Contractor estimate for foundation repair: $12,000.
Turn 15: Contractor estimate for interior basement drywall: $6,000.
Turn 16: Structural engineer report requested.
Turn 17: Structural engineer inspected basement exterior grading.
Turn 18: Engineer notes negative grading sloping toward house.
Turn 19: Exterior soil saturation high due to seasonal precipitation.
Turn 20: Engineer notes foundation cracks show historical efflorescence.
Turn 21: Efflorescence indicates ongoing moisture penetration.
Turn 22: Homeowner claims never noticed efflorescence before.
Turn 23: Adjuster reviewed policy declarations page for HO-0304.
Turn 24: Adjuster reviewed weather station rainfall data for the area.
Turn 25: 1.5 inches of rain recorded over 48-hour period.
Turn 26: Plumbing supply lines and waste pipes pressure-tested; no leak.
Turn 27: All internal plumbing fixtures confirmed fully intact.
Turn 28: Engineer preliminary report submitted to claims department.
Turn 29: Contractor submitted updated invoice for emergency shoring.
Turn 30: Adjuster preparing final file review for coverage determination.

destroyed_fact: Turn 11 fact: HVAC service technician confirmed compressor burned out due to intentional modification by uncertified third party.
turns: Turn 01: Claim reported: Commercial chiller compressor burnout.
Turn 02: Adjuster assigned: R. Davis.
Turn 03: Spoke with building facilities manager regarding breakdown.
Turn 04: Scheduled diagnostic inspection with certified HVAC technician.
Turn 05: Technician arrived on site at facility.
Turn 06: Power supply to main breaker tested at 480V 3-phase.
Turn 07: Electrical voltage found normal, no grid power surge detected.
Turn 08: Motor windings tested; direct ground fault detected in stator.
Turn 09: Compressor oil sample taken for spectrographic analysis.
Turn 10: Oil analysis shows metal filings and severe thermal breakdown.
Turn 11: CRITICAL FACT: Technician discovered safety bypass switch installed; uncertified third party intentionally bypassed refrigerant pressure cutouts.
Turn 12: Facilities manager questioned about bypass switch.
Turn 13: Manager claims outside contractor performed maintenance in May.
Turn 14: Replacement compressor quote obtained from Trane: $7,500.
Turn 15: Labor estimate for crane and installation: $2,000.
Turn 16: Adjuster cross-referenced Schedule A of HO-0308.
Turn 17: Chiller serial #CH-8802 listed on scheduled equipment.
Turn 18: Adjuster reviewed Section IV Exclusions for HO-0308.
Turn 19: Clause E-27 reviewed regarding wear and mechanical failure.
Turn 20: Clause E-28 checked for schedule verification.
Turn 21: Technician field report requested in writing.
Turn 22: Written technician report received by claims desk.
Turn 23: Technician notes bypass directly caused compressor seizure.
Turn 24: Maintenance logs reviewed from prior 12 months.
Turn 25: Logs confirm bypass was installed to keep unit running during leak.
Turn 26: Photos taken of bypassed high-pressure safety switch.
Turn 27: Second opinion requested from senior equipment specialist.
Turn 28: Equipment specialist concurs that bypass caused failure.
Turn 29: Final invoice from HVAC diagnostics company received: $450.
Turn 30: Adjuster finalizing adjudication report.
